en.headline: Customs seizes over 7000 suspected counterfeit items worth HK$7.6 million
en.dek: The two-week Time Shield operation targeting cross-boundary transshipment of fake watches and related goods yielded 16 cases and one arrest in Kwai Chung.
body: Hong Kong Customs seized around 7,000 items of suspected counterfeit goods, including watches, clothing and mobile phones, with an estimated market value of over HK$7.6 million during Operation Time Shield from 28 September to 13 October.

The operation detected 16 related cases involving cross-boundary transshipment. Customs believed the goods were destined for overseas markets. On 7 October officers arrested a 65-year-old man in an industrial unit in Kwai Chung and seized about 600 items worth about HK$400,000.
Investigations are ongoing. Customs said some seized watches were high-quality fakes of luxury brands and carried counterfeit boxes, certificates and receipts.
Under the Trade Descriptions Ordinance, dealing in counterfeit goods is an offence punishable by a maximum fine of HK$500,000 and five years’ imprisonment.

zh.headline: 海關「時盾」行動檢逾7000件懷疑冒牌貨 市值逾760萬元
zh.dek: 兩周行動打擊跨境轉運冒牌手錶等物品，偵破16宗案件，並在葵涌拘捕一名65歲男子。
body: 香港海關由9月28日至10月13日展開代號「時盾」的執法行動，打擊跨境轉運冒牌手錶及相關物品，檢獲約7000件懷疑冒牌貨物，包括手錶、服飾及手機，估計市值逾760萬元。
行動偵破16宗相關案件。海關相信有關貨物會轉口至海外。10月7日，人員在葵涌一個工廈單位拘捕一名65歲男子，並檢獲約600件懷疑冒牌物品，市值約40萬元。
調查仍在進行。海關指部分檢獲手錶為高仿奢侈品牌，並附有偽造錶盒、證書及單據。
根據《商品說明條例》，任何人進出口、銷售或管有冒牌物品即屬違法，一經定罪最高可被判罰款50萬元及監禁5年。
